The Milwaukee return has one calmer afternoon connection, while looping back to Minneapolis would require a long Thursday drive.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the upper Midwest recruitment loop from comparison into reservations.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize flights, request window seats where available, reserve the rental car, choose the three hotels, confirm queen-room availability, breakfast hours, parking, restaurant access, and assemble the airfare and lodging notes for reimbursement.
events.scenario_brief: Tessa's office approves the open-jaw plan because it avoids a Thursday backtrack across Wisconsin and Minnesota. She is ready to book a Sunday afternoon Salt Lake City-to-Minneapolis flight, a Thursday afternoon Milwaukee-to-Salt Lake City return with one connection, a rental car with room for boxes, and hotels near St. Paul or Roseville, Madison, and Milwaukee or Brookfield. The remaining details are room setup, breakfast timing before early starts, parking charges, nearby dinner options, and the note explaining the higher airfare.

events.continuity_hook: Handles final timing, weather, food, and materials logistics for the booked upper Midwest trip.
events.interaction_goal: Decide whether to keep the changed return or move to a later connection, add drive buffers between Wisconsin stops, set a quick breakfast plan for the Madison morning, update the Milwaukee arrival window, and make a concise packing, receipt, and materials-security checklist.
events.scenario_brief: The week before departure, the airline moves Tessa's Milwaukee connection earlier by enough to make the transfer feel tight, and an early winter forecast could slow the Tuesday and Wednesday drives. The Madison hotel also confirms breakfast starts after she needs to leave for a morning school visit, and the Milwaukee campus sends a separate materials drop-off gate for Thursday.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a personal holiday-planning thread after the last major fall recruitment trip.
events.interaction_goal: Compare flying versus driving for the Wednesday-to-Sunday window, identify practical hotel areas near the relatives, check two-queen rooms, breakfast, parking, and nearby food, and choose a return timing that protects Monday school and work.
events.scenario_brief: After the fall recruitment loop wraps up, Tessa's spouse's family confirms Thanksgiving in San Diego. The teens can leave after an early school release on Wednesday and need to be back Sunday night, but relatives have limited sleeping space, so a nearby hotel may be needed. Airfares are rising, the holiday return window is crowded, and the family needs to decide whether all four should fly, drive, or have only part of the family go.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Thanksgiving San Diego visit from fly-versus-drive comparison into booking choices.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the family flight plan, pick the safer Sunday return window, reserve a refundable two-queen hotel, confirm breakfast, parking, and nearby dinner options, and decide whether they need a rental car or can rely on relatives for local rides.
events.scenario_brief: The relatives confirm they can host meals but not four overnight guests, and the family decides the Wednesday-to-Sunday drive is too draining. The workable air options are a Wednesday late-afternoon Salt Lake City-to-San Diego nonstop and either a Sunday late-afternoon or evening return; fares have risen enough that Tessa wants the hotel choice and baggage plan settled before booking. A refundable two-queen hotel near the relatives includes breakfast and parking, while a closer holiday hotel has tighter cancellation terms and weaker food access.

events.continuity_hook: Handles the final practical details for the booked San Diego holiday weekend.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm the Wednesday airport departure time, adjust seats where possible, add the late-arrival note, verify the two-queen room and holiday breakfast hours, confirm parking, and set a Sunday leave-by time for the return flight.
events.scenario_brief: A few days before the Thanksgiving trip, the hotel asks Tessa to add a late-arrival note for Wednesday, and the airline app shows the family's seats split across rows with limited window availability. Relatives move Friday lunch earlier, and the Sunday return still works if they leave the family gathering by mid-afternoon. She only needs a quick check on airport timing, room guarantee, and meals.

events.continuity_hook: Shifts from holiday family travel into winter professional travel planning.
events.interaction_goal: Compare a Sunday afternoon flight, a Monday morning flight, and driving; weigh the official block against nearby breakfast-included hotels; identify transportation, meal, and receipt issues; and decide which refundable hotel rooms should be held.
events.scenario_brief: After the holiday weekend, Tessa is asked to attend a January admissions operations workshop in downtown Denver with a Monday 1:00 p.m. kickoff, a Tuesday full-day agenda, and a Wednesday 11:30 a.m. closing session. The university will reimburse either air or mileage, but winter driving across Wyoming looks unpredictable, and the official hotel block is convenient but does not include breakfast and charges a high parking fee. Nearby hotels are cheaper and include breakfast but may add cold-weather walks or rideshares.

events.continuity_hook: Turns the Denver workshop comparison into flight and hotel selections.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the Sunday and Wednesday flights, request window seats where available, choose between the conference hotel and nearby suite-style option, confirm breakfast and nearby dinner access, plan ground transportation, and draft the reimbursement note for any above-cap room rate.
events.scenario_brief: The workshop agenda confirms that Monday's opening session includes required check-in by 12:30 p.m., making same-day flight arrival too risky. A Sunday afternoon nonstop to Denver and a Wednesday afternoon return fit the office schedule, while the official hotel block is now above the normal nightly cap unless the conference-rate note is attached. A nearby suite-style hotel still has refundable queen rooms with breakfast, but Tessa needs to weigh the walk to the meeting site against the simpler reimbursement path.

events.continuity_hook: Closes the Denver workshop planning thread with weather, timing, and arrival logistics.
events.interaction_goal: Decide whether to keep the shifted outbound or move earlier, set the Salt Lake City airport cutoff, choose rideshare or rail from the airport, plan Sunday dinner, confirm receipt handling, and make a concise packing checklist.
events.scenario_brief: The week before the Denver workshop, a storm system is forecast for the Front Range on Sunday night, and the airline posts a small schedule shift on the outbound that still keeps the afternoon departure workable. The hotel confirms breakfast starts early enough on workshop mornings, but its restaurant closes early on Sunday, and the workshop sends a digital badge pickup window. Tessa wants a final travel-day risk check rather than a full rework.

events.continuity_hook: Starts the first spring yield road swing after the winter conference trip.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the full-drive, Boise round-trip, and open-jaw flight plans; sketch the Boise, Twin Falls, and Pocatello overnight sequence; identify hotel areas with breakfast, parking, and restaurant access; and flag the airfare, rental car, weather, and materials-handling points needed before approval.
events.scenario_brief: Once the Denver workshop wraps, Tessa receives the late-February Idaho yield plan: a Tuesday evening admitted-student reception in Boise, a Wednesday 7:30 a.m. counselor breakfast in Nampa, a Wednesday afternoon transfer table in Twin Falls, and a Thursday morning high-school visit near Pocatello. She needs to decide whether to drive the whole route from Salt Lake City with materials, fly into Boise and rent a car, or use an open-jaw return from Idaho Falls; winter roads, materials boxes, and early breakfast logistics are the main unresolved pieces.

events.continuity_hook: Narrows the Idaho route after the initial fly-versus-drive comparison.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the drive plan, set the overnight sequence, compare Boise/Meridian/Nampa and Pocatello hotel areas, identify which refundable rooms to hold, and note parking, breakfast timing, nearby dinner, and materials storage needs.
events.scenario_brief: The admissions office approves the Idaho swing as a mileage trip rather than flying, because Tessa has two boxes of admitted-student materials and the Boise-to-Idaho Falls rental plan would add one-way fees. The Tuesday Boise reception is moved to a downtown venue with garage parking, the Wednesday Nampa counselor breakfast is confirmed for 7:30 a.m., the Twin Falls transfer table will run until 4:30 p.m., and the Thursday Pocatello visit stays at 8:30 a.m. The unresolved choice is whether to drive up from Salt Lake City Tuesday morning with a weather buffer, hold a Monday-night cancellable room, and whether Tuesday night should be in Boise, Meridian, or Nampa.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Idaho swing from route choice into reservations and travel-day logistics.
events.interaction_goal: Book or hold the Nampa and Pocatello hotels, verify room setup, breakfast hours, parking, and cancellation windows, map the materials handoff points, and assemble the mileage, parking, and meal receipt plan.
events.scenario_brief: Tessa decides to keep the full-drive plan and hold a Monday weather room only if the forecast worsens. The best Tuesday-night option is now a Nampa hotel with early breakfast and free parking, while the cheaper Boise property would add a longer morning drive; in Pocatello, the practical hotel near Thursday's high-school visit has restaurant access but limited room-type inventory. The remaining pieces are reservation timing, a realistic Wednesday drive from Nampa to Twin Falls to Pocatello, and a concise reimbursement explanation for taking the car instead of a flight.

events.continuity_hook: Handles the final weather, food, and materials details for the Idaho swing.
events.interaction_goal: Decide whether to add the Monday-night weather-buffer room or leave early Tuesday, set drive cutoffs and fuel stops, adjust the materials drop and Nampa arrival plan, choose a simple Wednesday dinner option near Pocatello, and make a short packing, receipts, and winter-road checklist.
events.scenario_brief: Two days before departure, the I-84 forecast shows a snow band between Burley and Twin Falls on Tuesday morning, and the Boise reception venue pushes the materials drop window to 3:30 p.m. The Nampa hotel can prepare a grab-and-go breakfast before the counselor event, but the Pocatello restaurant closest to the hotel is closed Wednesday night. Tessa wants to avoid rebuilding the trip unless the Tuesday drive becomes too tight.

events.continuity_hook: Starts the next spring yield trip after the Idaho travel wraps.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the open-jaw and round-trip flight plans, identify reasonable arrival and return windows, sketch the hotel areas for Plano/Fort Worth and Austin, flag breakfast and late-dinner logistics around the events, and list the approval questions on airfare, rental car, and materials handling.
events.scenario_brief: After the Idaho swing, Tessa is assigned a mid-March Texas yield mini-loop with a Tuesday evening admitted-student reception in Plano, a Wednesday morning counselor breakfast in Fort Worth, and a Thursday late-afternoon transfer and alumni meetup in Austin. Materials can be shipped to Plano but not to Austin, reimbursement favors one rental car over separate rideshares, and she needs to be back in Salt Lake City before Friday evening family commitments. The unresolved choice is whether to fly into Dallas/Fort Worth and home from Austin, keep a Dallas round trip with a long drive back, or shorten the Austin piece.

versions.boundary_condition: This is a soft preference: Delta is favored only among otherwise suitable options and may coexist with other acceptable preferred carriers.
versions.condition: When choosing among flight carriers and Delta is available while also satisfying the trip's schedule, route, price, and stop constraints.
versions.default_action: Search for or present Delta options as part of the preferred carrier set, and favor Delta when it is otherwise comparable to alternatives.
versions.exception_condition: Use another acceptable carrier when Delta is unavailable, materially worse, or does not meet the current trip constraints.
versions.name: soft_delta_preferred_carrier
versions.preference_value: Delta is a preferred airline to include in the flight shortlist, but not an exclusive carrier requirement.
versions.scope_condition: Applies to her self-booked U.S. flights from Salt Lake City for recruitment loops, conferences, and occasional family trips.

versions.boundary_condition: Applies only to flight departure time-of-day. Do not infer it for arrival times, dates, routes, every leg automatically, or earliest-afternoon departures as a recurring rule.
versions.condition: When selecting or comparing flight departure times.
versions.default_action: Look first for departure options in the afternoon; follow any current explicit request for another time window or exact time.
versions.exception_condition: If acceptable afternoon departures are unavailable or conflict with other stated constraints, ask before broadening to nearby time windows.
versions.name: prefers_afternoon_departures
versions.preference_value: Prefers flight departures in the afternoon when no different departure-time constraint is specified.
versions.scope_condition: Applies when choosing flight departure times for trips without a fixed competing time constraint, especially after morning school visits, campus meetings, or office handoffs.

versions.boundary_condition: Do not infer that the user always wants nonstop first, wants a layover for price reasons, or wants to add a stop to break up a long route unless the current request says so.
versions.condition: When evaluating flight itineraries where a connection is acceptable, necessary, or being considered.
versions.default_action: Favor itineraries with at most one short layover; ask before selecting itineraries with multiple layovers or a long layover.
versions.exception_condition: Override this default if the user explicitly requests nonstop only, requests a longer stopover, or prioritizes schedule, availability, price, or another constraint over layover count or layover duration.
versions.name: flight_single_short_layover_preference
versions.preference_value: Prefers connecting itineraries with no more than one layover, and for any layover to be short enough for a comfortable transfer rather than prolonged.
versions.scope_condition: Applies to domestic itineraries where a connection is being considered, especially routes from Salt Lake City to smaller recruitment or conference markets.

versions.boundary_condition: Applies only to seat location. If seat selection is unavailable at booking or is deferred until check-in, note that limitation and try to secure a window seat at the earliest available time.
versions.condition: When booking or selecting seats for flights where a seat location preference can be applied.
versions.default_action: Prefer or request a window seat by default.
versions.exception_condition: Use a different seat only if the user specifies another seat preference, needs a different seating arrangement, or no acceptable window seat is available.
versions.name: prefers_window_seat_on_flights
versions.scope_condition: Applies to seat selection on flights she books for herself, including solo work trips and occasional family travel.

versions.boundary_condition: Use this as a soft preference, not an absolute requirement, because the evidence ranges from a direct requirement to a tentative request and a later verification question.
versions.condition: When evaluating or booking a hotel, treat free breakfast as a recurring included-service preference.
versions.default_action: Prioritize or verify hotels with free breakfast when available; if breakfast is not listed, ask or check rather than assuming it is included.
versions.exception_condition: Do not reject an otherwise suitable hotel solely for lacking free breakfast unless the user explicitly makes it required in the current booking; do not infer a full or high-quality breakfast requirement unless stated.
versions.name: prefer_included_hotel_breakfast
versions.preference_value: Prefer hotels that include free breakfast.
versions.scope_condition: Applies to hotels for early-start recruitment, conference, and short family stays where breakfast logistics are part of the comparison.

versions.boundary_condition: Do not infer specific cuisine, star rating, bar service, kid-friendliness, downtown location, ski access, or wooded setting unless stated for the current trip.
versions.condition: When searching for, comparing, or summarizing hotel options.
versions.default_action: Mention on-site or nearby restaurant availability and use convenient dining access as a soft tie-breaker rather than a hard filter.
versions.exception_condition: Do not apply if the user explicitly deprioritizes dining access or if stronger current-trip constraints override it.
versions.name: hotel_restaurant_access
versions.preference_value: Hotels with on-site or nearby restaurant access, with restaurant availability noted during comparisons.
versions.scope_condition: Applies to hotels after evening fairs, receptions, late arrivals, or suburban venue stays where convenient dinner access matters.

versions.boundary_condition: Evidence supports queen-size beds as the recurring preference. A king bed may be acceptable when explicitly offered or requested, but the evidence does not establish a reusable preference to upgrade to king whenever possible.
versions.condition: When booking a standard hotel room where a single larger/shared bed is appropriate and no separate-bed setup has been requested.
versions.default_action: Filter for or request a queen-size bed when bed type is selectable; if the listing only shows double, twin, or unspecified bedding, confirm the bed setup before booking.
versions.exception_condition: Honor explicit requests for twin beds, multiple separate beds, multiple rooms with different bedding, accessibility-related bedding, or any other trip-specific bed arrangement.
versions.name: queen_bed_for_single_bed_hotel_rooms
versions.preference_value: Prefer a queen-size bed for hotel rooms intended to have one larger/shared bed.
versions.scope_condition: Applies to standard hotel rooms for solo work travel or spouse/family weekend stays when a single larger-bed room is the appropriate setup.
